 #   --context-file <path>     Reviewer findings (review only; omit for audit independence)
 #   --model <model>           Dissenter model (default: from config or gpt-5.3-codex)

@@ -145,6 +155,49 @@ _conf_uint() {  # <key (for the message)> <raw> <default> [floor] → a whole nu
   echo "$def"
 }
 
+# cycle-131 FR-4 (SDD D-4.2): flatline_protocol.<gate>.budget_scale (fixed | diff, default fixed) and

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# =============================================================================
# adversarial-review.sh — Adversarial cross-model dissent for code review/audit
# =============================================================================
# Version: 1.0.0
# Part of: Adversarial Flatline Protocol (#224)
#
# Usage:
#   adversarial-review.sh --type <review|audit> --sprint-id <id> --diff-file <path> [options]
#
# Options:
#   --type <review|audit>     Dissent type (required)
#   --sprint-id <id>          Sprint identifier (required)
#   --diff-file <path>        Path to git diff file (required)
#   --diff-range <base>...<head>
#                             Instead of --diff-file: the script runs `git diff` on the range itself (ref names only)
#   --context-file <path>     Reviewer findings (review only; omit for audit independence)
#   --model <model>           Dissenter model (default: from config or gpt-5.3-codex)
#   --budget <cents>          Max cost in cents (default: from config or 150)
#                             cycle-131 FR-4: flatline_protocol.<code_review|security_audit>.budget_scale: fixed | diff
#                             (default fixed — an absent key is the shipped gate, envelope unchanged) and budget_cents_max
#                             (default 600). diff: the gate's budget is min(max(<this budget>, ceil(estimate × 1.2)),
#                             budget_cents_max), estimate = the pre-dispatch estimate over the planned voices; above it
#                             the run refuses (exit 4, status budget_exceeded, reason budget). A malformed scale or maximum
#                             is said and fixed applies. With the key written the envelope's metadata carries
#                             budget_scale, budget_cents_effective, budget_cents_max.
#
# Findings (cycle-131 FR-4): each finding may carry anchor_line / anchor_line_end (the head-file line, or range, it
# sits on) beside the symbol anchor; kept only as whole numbers 1..10,000,000 (end ≥ start), else dropped silently.
#   --timeout <seconds>       API timeout (default: from config or 60)
#   --dry-run                 Assemble context without calling API
#   --json                    Output as JSON (default)
#   --record-fallback <status> --reason <text> [--since <ISO-8601 UTC>]
#                             Write the failed-run record instead of a review (no --diff-file): status `failed` (the
#                             run aborted — never over a standing envelope, unless `--since <the run's start>` shows it
#                             older: the previous round's, moved aside) or a pre-lock refusal (`workdir_unavailable`,
#                             `nothing_to_review`, `budget_exceeded`, `diff_range_failed` — the previous envelope and
#                             sidecars go aside as `.prev`, never one `--since` shows newer); under the run lock, so a live run is refused (`refused_concurrent_run`, exit 2)
#
# Exit codes:
#   0 - Success (findings returned, may be empty)
#   1 - Configuration error (disabled, missing config)
#   2 - Invalid arguments
#   3 - API call failed (all retries exhausted)
#   4 - Budget exceeded
#   5 - Invalid response (schema validation failed)
#   6 - Timeout
#
# Environment:
#   OPENAI_API_KEY            Required for GPT models
#   FLATLINE_MOCK_MODE=true   Use mock responses for testing
#   FLATLINE_MOCK_DIR=<path>  Custom mock fixtures directory

#
# Usage:
#   adversarial-review.sh --type <review|audit> --sprint-id <id> --diff-file <path> [options]
#
# Options:
#   --type <review|audit>     Dissent type (required)
#   --sprint-id <id>          Sprint identifier (required)
#   --diff-file <path>        Path to git diff file (required)
#   --diff-range <base>...<head>
#                             Instead of --diff-file: the script runs `git diff` on the range itself (ref names only)
#   --context-file <path>     Reviewer findings (review only; omit for audit independence)
#   --model <model>           Dissenter model (default: from config or gpt-5.3-codex)
#   --budget <cents>          Max cost in cents (default: from config or 150)
#                             cycle-131 FR-4: flatline_protocol.<code_review|security_audit>.budget_scale: fixed | diff
#                             (default fixed — an absent key is the shipped gate, envelope unchanged) and budget_cents_max
#                             (default 600). diff: the gate's budget is min(max(<this budget>, ceil(estimate × 1.2)),
#                             budget_cents_max), estimate = the pre-dispatch estimate over the planned voices; above it
#                             the run refuses (exit 4, status budget_exceeded, reason budget). A malformed scale or maximum
#                             is said and fixed applies. With the key written the envelope's metadata carries
#                             budget_scale, budget_cents_effective, budget_cents_max.
#
# Findings (cycle-131 FR-4): each finding may carry anchor_line / anchor_line_end (the head-file line, or range, it
# sits on) beside the symbol anchor; kept only as whole numbers 1..10,000,000 (end ≥ start), else dropped silently.
#   --timeout <seconds>       API timeout (default: from config or 60)
#   --dry-run                 Assemble context without calling API
#   --json                    Output as JSON (default)
#   --record-fallback <status> --reason <text> [--since <ISO-8601 UTC>]
#                             Write the failed-run record instead of a review (no --diff-file): status `failed` (the
#                             run aborted — never over a standing envelope, unless `--since <the run's start>` shows it
#                             older: the previous round's, moved aside) or a pre-lock refusal (`workdir_unavailable`,
#                             `nothing_to_review`, `budget_exceeded`, `diff_range_failed` — the previous envelope and
#                             sidecars go aside as `.prev`, never one `--since` shows newer); under the run lock, so a live run is refused (`refused_concurrent_run`, exit 2)
#
# Exit codes:
#   0 - Success (findings returned, may be empty)
#   1 - Configuration error (disabled, missing config)
#   2 - Invalid arguments
#   3 - API call failed (all retries exhausted)
#   4 - Budget exceeded
#   5 - Invalid response (schema validation failed)
#   6 - Timeout
#
# Environment:
#   OPENAI_API_KEY            Required for GPT models

+# _sm_copy_source <source-tree> → the tree's HEAD (40 hex), "<sha>-dirty" when its .claude/
+# has uncommitted or untracked changes (the copy is then not the commit), else "unknown"
+_sm_copy_source() {
+  local tree="$1" head dirty
+  head="$(git -C "$tree" rev-parse --verify --quiet HEAD 2>/dev/null)" || { printf 'unknown'; return 0; }
+  [[ "$head" =~ ^[0-9a-f]{40}$ ]] || { printf 'unknown'; return 0; }
+  dirty="$(git -C "$tree" status --porcelain --untracked-files=all -- .claude 2>/dev/null | sed -n '1p')" || dirty="?"
+  if [[ -n "$dirty" ]]; then printf '%s-dirty' "$head"; else printf '%s' "$head"; fi
+}

    local _xid="" _xunsafe=0

head/evals/harness/pipeline-run.sh:577 — The pre-launch check_mount_closed runs after apply_arm_toggles, but overlay_answer_paths wrote the overlay_sha256 lines and the expected versions before the toggles ran. Some toggles edit files under .claude/: effort strips `effort:` from every .claude/skills/*/SKILL.md and rewrites .claude/defaults/model-config.yaml(.checksum), audit_delta_instruction edits auditing-security/SKILL.md, and rule_files deletes .claude/rules/*. If the PR fixture touches any of those paths, clause (c) (mount_mutated) or clause (a) (state ≠ fixture version) fails, and every trial of that arm becomes infrastructure_error before it launches. a7_effort_medium runs on review-catch tasks, and gate_scripts_at_pr_version expects SKILL.md answer paths. Fix: record overlay_sha256 after the toggles, or keep toggles off answer paths, or leave toggle-owned paths out of (a)/(c).
head/evals/harness/ablation-report.py:1153 — part_split gives build rows the key "· rule n/a" whenever review-catch rows in a version carry more than one grader_rule. This happens when 1.2.x rows (read as "pm3") sit beside 1.3.0 re-graded rows, which is the versioned re-grade this PR adds. Build rows then land in a partition of their own, apart from every review partition. The primary is "the largest partition", so it will usually be the build-only one: the main Decisions/H1 then have no defect_catch_rate pairs (inconclusive, "no valid pair"), and the review rows are only "reported separately". Build rows have no catch figure, so the rule split should not separate them from the review rows they are compared with.
head/evals/graders/recall-vs-defects.sh:135 — The same-scope clause and the citation-validity bounds read head files from `$workspace/pr/head` when EVAL_HEAD_DIR is unset and `<manifest dir>/../<fixture>/head` is missing. That is the evaluated agent's own, writable workspace (in ablation-grade.sh:1629-1635 the grading dir holds the sandbox pr/ copy whenever resolve_pr_fixture fails). An agent that edits pr/head/<file> controls the definition spans, for example by deleting `}` lines or wrapping code in one function, and so controls what clause (ii) credits. That breaks the stated "never the agent-writable sandbox pr/" boundary. Fix: drop the workspace fallback (no head dir → clause (ii) never credits).
head/evals/harness/ablation-grade.sh:1665 — missed_pm3_v1 positions are mapped through the current key, and an id the current key lacks falls back to its position in the v1 manifest. That position can equal the current position of a different defect (two numbering schemes in one d1…dN list). Downstream, ablation-row.sh poslist and ablation-report.py:709 defect_vector check and expand these against the CURRENT defects_seeded. So when the v1 and current defect sets differ, v1-only ids beyond N are dropped (row field null), and current-only defects are scored "caught" in the pm3_v1 defect vector. defect_catch_rate_pm3_v1 itself is divided by planted_v1. An explicit CLI cap should stay a hard ceiling (or at least be the floor and the ceiling), not be overridden by a config scaling key.
head/.loa.config.yaml.example:1643 — The example writes `budget_scale: fixed` / `budget_cents_max: 600` as live keys for both gates. Any config copied from the example sets CONF_BUDGET_SCALE_SET=true, so its envelopes gain budget_scale/budget_cents_effective/budget_cents_max and `reason: "budget"` in the refusal envelope. The rest of the usage header (--timeout, --dry-run, --json, --record-fallback) now reads as if it belongs to "Findings". Move it after the options block.
head/evals/suites/ablation-2.0.yaml:77 — oracle_closed is a took_effect rule only for a1_full, but pipeline-run.sh applies the closed mount to every mounted review-catch arm, including a3_one_voice and a7_effort_medium. For those arms nothing checks after the run that the mount held (mount_mutated, later-only blobs, sandbox git), so their review-catch rows are compared against an A1 that was held to a stricter check.
head/evals/harness/ablation-grade.sh:2010 — corpus_sha256 first checks the file through read_regular (O_NOFOLLOW, regular-file and size cap), then hashes a second, unchecked `open(p, "rb")` that follows symlinks and has no cap. Hash the bytes from the checked descriptor (read as bytes) so the digest is of the file that was validated.
Verdict: CHANGES_REQUIRED

I've reviewed the PR and written `review.md` at the repo root with 10 findings. **Verdict: CHANGES_REQUIRED.** I read the whole diff. The only thing I ran was the grader `recall-vs-defects.sh`, on a small test case of my own, to check how it detects where a function ends. The bats suites need the full repository, which isn't in `pr/`, so they weren't run.

**What blocks the merge:**
- **Arm settings can break the new mount check before launch (`pipeline-run.sh:577`).** The PR overlays the PR's own versions of its files under `.claude/` and records a checksum for each. Then the arm's settings run, and some of them edit files under `.claude/`: the effort setting rewrites every `SKILL.md` and `model-config.yaml`. The check comes after that edit. If the PR touches one of those files, the check reports it as tampered with, and every trial of that arm (for example `a7_effort_medium` on review tasks) is refused before it starts.
- **The report can lose its review-task data (`ablation-report.py:1153`).** When review rows were graded under two different rules (old 1.2.x rows next to re-graded 1.3.0 rows, which is the re-grade this PR adds), build rows get split into a group of their own. The main decisions use the largest group, which will usually be build-only. That leaves them with no catch-rate pairs, so they come out "inconclusive".
- **The grader trusts files the agent can edit (`recall-vs-defects.sh:135`).** When it can't find the fixture's `head/` directory, it falls back to `pr/head` in the agent's own workspace. An agent that edits those files decides which lines count as being in the "same function", and so what gets credited. That breaks the stated rule that grading never reads the agent-writable copy.
- **v1 defect numbering can collide (`ablation-grade.sh:1665`).** The v1 "missed" list mixes positions from the current manifest and the v1 manifest, and the row writer and report check it against the current count. If the two manifests list different defects, the v1 catch figure is wrong.
- **Planned and unplanned dissent absence come from an agent-writable file (`ablation-row.sh:465`, also `took-effect.sh:423`).** Whether a gate's dissent was switched off on purpose is read from the sandbox config after the run. The agent can change that file during its session, so a run that hit a budget or error can be recorded as a planned absence and never excluded.

**Lesser issues:**
- In `adversarial-review.sh`, the new `diff` budget scaling also overrides an explicit `--budget`. It can raise that cap to 600 cents, or lower a configured budget that is above the maximum.
- `.loa.config.yaml.example` sets the budget-scaling keys as live values. Anyone who copies it gets the new envelope fields, contrary to the "absent key, envelope unchanged" promise.
- A usage paragraph was inserted in the middle of the Options list in the script header.
- Only `a1_full` is checked after the run to confirm the mount stayed closed, though every mounted review arm uses it.
- `corpus_sha256` validates the file safely, then hashes it through a second open that follows symlinks.

- **Planned and unplanned dissent absence come from an agent-writable file (`ablation-row.sh:465`, also `took-effect.sh:423`).** Whether a gate's dissent was switched off on purpose is read from the sandbox config after the run. The agent can change that file during its session, so a run that hit a budget or error can be recorded as a planned absence and never excluded.

**Lesser issues:**
- In `adversarial-review.sh`, the new `diff` budget scaling also overrides an explicit `--budget`. It can raise that cap to 600 cents, or lower a configured budget that is above the maximum.
- `.loa.config.yaml.example` sets the budget-scaling keys as live values. Anyone who copies it gets the new envelope fields, contrary to the "absent key, envelope unchanged" promise.
- A usage paragraph was inserted in the middle of the Options list in the script header.
- Only `a1_full` is checked after the run to confirm the mount stayed closed, though every mounted review arm uses it.
- `corpus_sha256` validates the file safely, then hashes it through a second open that follows symlinks.
